editorText:
When Tex came to, he could barely track his hands. He felt himself being reborn into his skin and thoughts as his now AI-assisted HUD lit up the ship around him. It had already tapped into his retinal wiring. Everything in his mind could read now, although his body felt cold.

He lay there, turned on his side, feeling himself awakening from what seemed like a bad dream. All he remembered was floating in the black of space, the rear of Tex's Mark IV with a recovery harpoon aimed, lockjawed. "Send my condolences to my family," he had said as he pulled the trigger. A bright light shone, blinding him. That was all he could remember; everything went blank after that.

Nonetheless, he felt safe. A strange figure seemed to appear in the distance. He floated in the regenerative tank, preparing for the lighter gravity. The reduced weight on his body brought strange thoughts or a distorted vision of a planet. John had just awoken from a dream—one of a planet with shifting surfaces. The horizon was a series of rich reds, oranges, and a dark purple silhouette that topped them, all overlooked by a transitioning bed of stars.

He suddenly found himself running, trying to keep his balance. Rolling hills, like floating bodies, came toward him, then the sound of breaking, crushing rocks overpowered him. He felt his feet being pulled down into the abyss, and then he shot back up, landing on one brace gracefully. Although he wasn't in his Mark IV suit, he had become something else. Something different, it was all coming back to him, but he couldn’t make out why it was taking him so long. He couldn’t even recognise the ship he was in. “Icarus?” He mumbled as he looked around the hardened exterior shell of the Beverly.

"We've been in a deep sleep, Captain," said Tau. Side effects are normal when you awake, just allow some time for your neural network to re-establish itself. I reccommend the piano myself personally, it will have you back to good in no time”. Tau chuckled.

“It’s fine Tau, I can recognise that chuckle a mile off, How’s Tex, he took quite a blow”, “He’s doing fine, you will see him soon enough”., “God, why does my head hurt so much”, “Tebo mentioned something to do with the ” Tau was soft in her words, with a distinct confidence. “The neural bridge when we passed through caused some delays in processing of our past. The neural bridge digs deep into hard wiring and muscle memory within the mind, re-imagining traumatic events in ways without violence”, John took a moment to absorb what Tau was telling him.

“You mean to say that Tebo has taken us all through a , that has potentially messed with our heads and reprogrammed our thinking”, “Well yes if you want to get to the bottom of it that sums it up, not to worry though, according to Tebo only some small variance, a total of 2%, the change was in you, but the others they’re not feeling anything, and Tex, well things were interesting with Tex, Tebo explained he would cover it in the debrief later”.

“Geez this is a lot to wake up to” John thought to himself as he gazed down at his what resembled his feet, in a way he admired the intricacy of the design. He had never seen pneumatic s like it before, from a generation ahead of it’s time they seemed, but not of his time, something further.”

The room door where Tau and John had been so peacefully getting reaquanted opened faster that John could feel the tinglng sensation coming back to what felt like toes attached to his extremeties. Although they weren’t, they were tools, with thousands of wired and excited connections, It was as though he had never lost his initial body, and the neural integration felt flawless.

“Ahh yes the Doctors work is always astonishes me, beholder of the eye that man” A Joyous voice of enthusiasm trickled through the room as Tebo entered. “Don’t worry about the reset John… Here, this will help”, Tebo handed John a glass of water. Although when he drank it he felt a sudden rush. He was being drawn back into his subconscious. He remembered what felt like the last 3 months in an instant. And immediately he knew what had to be done.

“Thanks Tebo.. How are we looking on the belly of the Beverly”, “Systems are running operational.. We are down about 200 rounds from the mounted Storm rail, although we can replenish that rather quickly, I intercepted an asteroid belt on the way while you were all sleeping, and with out cargo hold we can fit a couple rocks, They have already been broken down and prints of the munitions carried out, stock has been completely replenished”.

“It’s not like we will be needing them anytime soon, hopefully” said Tau. John walked over to the bridge looking out into deep space, He could see a strange planet dawning in the bridge window like a pink blossom. It’s atmosphere a beautiful dancing silhouette of purples reds pinks and on occasion the soft spec of green broke through from the planets surface. “Yes” said John, let’s take some time to pull our heads together..” John turned to face Tebo. “Thank you Tebo for this most auspicious drink. A moment alone with Lieutenant Vang”, “Don’t mind me John. I will see you on the deck for debrief in 20 minutes”, “Tebo” John interrupted once more as Tebo began to exit the room. “Yes Chief” Tebo paused in his tracks. “Thank you” John bowled to Tebo with formidable respect, Tebo met his bowl in kind “Pleasure is all mine John”.

With Tebo’s exit the bridge fell quiet once more. “Where are the others” said John. “Tex is in the medical bay with Shai undergoing limb growth therapy”. Tau seemed sad in her statement, moved by her words John tried to reassure her “Shai knows what she is doing, he will make a full recovery”, He patted her on the shoulder. “If you are sure of it I trust your call” she said. Now they were finally alone.

“She handled herself well down there” “You’ve taken a liking to her I see” Tau seemed sarcastic but withdrawn in her comment. Then she continued diggin gdeeper into John’s pshyche. “So how far back exavtly do you remember cap?”, John was silent for a moment. “I remember the beverly.. But not as she is now”, “what do you mean John, like a different configuration”, “Yeah strange I know, it’s like these memories had been hidden or something, and the  has either implanted them or they have come rushing back”, “Shai did mention there could be side effects with the jump, she really quizzed that poor little frenchman”. John seemed disturbed still like something wasn’t adding up.

 “No these are real, I can remember the control sticks, they were completely different, The ship had been fitted out for strict scientific work, Jump work specifically, which is strange, my father never had anything to do with this technology, maybe it was another department under his wing”. “That is strange, I thought the old girl was just another hauler. I mean she certainly has a kick to her. Whatever program funded her was definitely government and at the front of it’s time and hauling ass”, “Yeah and there is just something about the seats, it feels almost as if you are in the womb” John paused there was an awkward silence “Do you remember.. Anything about your mother John”.. John was quick to respond, “Yeah, I remember her quite well.. Well parts of her, she was so driven with her work I hardly got to see her through the week afternoons, she was much like my father I guess, but I remember the weekends, checking the fence lines along the orchard to make sure the horses hadn’t gotten in. You can’t see the sun like it was back then now. Too much pollution. We were fortunate to grow up in such a time” John tapped at the port  window of the med bay. A dull thudding reverberated around it’s quartz shell but nothing more, sharp to the touch of his hardened finger tips. “And soon we will be seeing the dawn of 3 stars” Tau wandered over to the port window closest to John, she slowed as she approached the window, her gaze fixed on the black side of Oasis

“It won’t be long now till we couple with the Ignotius” Tau seemed weary in her comment, like she was repressing something deep inside her. “A new Dawn” said John softly. Tau rested her heavy head on John’s shoulder, her hand gently resting on his arm, as she watched on while the dark side of the new mysterious planet slowly revealed continents unknown to man.

“Tell me more about your father…” The dim light that just seemed to creep reaching past the dark surface of the planet before them seemed to sparkle ever so gently in John’s eyes, and she felt his sorrow, as they landed like drops that crashed with nothing but stillness in a cold dead black lake. “I remember his thoroughness, the way he always directed me toward this notion that flying had deeper meaning, that we weren’t just flying for ourselves, we were flying for the people..” John paused for a moment and lifted his arm around Tau warming her gently. “Then he focused his notion toward something else, He explained that he had found a way to make us better, more than human… He stopped spending time with me in simulations, he seemed to be drifting in another mental realm to our own, He called this place Oasis, that it was like Nirvana was to the Buddhist, Jerusalem to the Christians and Muslim, although the way he described it was, that he had found a way to take the human race to another realm beyond themselves and that only through implementing this and proving it could he save us” John seemed distressed the more he recalled everything. “After that I don’t remember much, he became a shell within this Oasis. I was left to fend for the two younger sisters and rear them in a world on the brink of social collapse with imminent fall to the machines final resistance waves.” “Yeah that hit fast. I remember, total lockdown, martial law. The handover felt like a massacre” “The strange thing was I never met any of these machines, we were just shown DZ target zones, all of which were often riddled with collateral, did the Commander care, no they were deserters in his eyes, lost to the cause of a vicious opponent hell bent on destroying what was left of us”
